description: Multi-Scale Tissue Regeneration Dynamics Across 6 Coupled Phases (Cycle 2A)

trauma_benchmarks.defect_name: Tier I: Deep Dermal Laceration with Minor Nerve Defect

evaluations.defect: Tier I: Deep Dermal Laceration with Minor Nerve Defect
evaluations.methodological_caveat: Biomarker presence (e.g. Pax7, TGF-beta3, VEGF) is NOT causally sufficient for functional regeneration. Axonal elongation remains strictly bound to 1.0-2.0 mm/day by tubulin transport. Volumetric muscle loss >5mm results in permanent functional deficit in unassisted adult humans.

scientific_conclusions.temporal_hierarchy: Wound healing exhibits rigid physical time decoupling: vascularization occurs in days (4-8d), epithelial dermal closure occurs in 1-2 weeks, but functional muscle and nerve regeneration spans 2 to 6 months. Combat-ready instantaneous healing is a biological impossibility.
scientific_conclusions.volumetric_muscle_loss_wall: For Tier III trauma (45 cm^3 volumetric muscle loss), standard human biology achieves only 25-35% functional recovery due to fibrotic cavity collapse (VML barrier). Acomys-like dermal mechanisms do NOT solve large mammalian skeletal muscle loss.
scientific_conclusions.nerve_regeneration_bottleneck: For a 90 mm nerve defect, axonal contact with target endplates requires at least 56 to 86 days even under the most optimistic biological growth velocity (1.5-2.0 mm/day). Target muscle motor endplates undergo progressive irreversible atrophy if denervated beyond 12-18 months.
